$comment: Golden vectors for ONE canonical spelling of a Team server URL, and the file its token lives in.
Both halves of this product derive these independently — `TeamServerAuth` in C#
(src_mcp/runners/Reviewers/TeamServerAuth.cs) and `teamServers.ts` in the extension — because the
extension WRITES the token file and the MCP shim READS it. They must agree exactly. If they do not,
a person signs in successfully and is told they are not signed in one second later, signs in again,
and it happens again: the extension wrote a1b2....token and the shim looked for c3d4....token.
Isolated unit tests on each side cannot catch that, because each side is self-consistent. Only a
shared fixture can, which is why this file exists outside both of them and is asserted by both
suites. Raised twice on the plan round of epic 3 (codex and gemini, independently).
`fingerprint` is the first 16 hex characters of sha256(canonical), lower-case. The token file is

vectors.why: the pair that motivated this — the panel saves a trailing slash, a vendor row usually has none
a default port is not part of the identity; the same server written both ways is one server
scheme and host are case-insensitive by the URL spec, so two spellings are one server
http keeps its own default port rule, and is a DIFFERENT server from the https one
a NON-default port is part of the identity: two servers on one host are two servers
a path is part of the identity — a server may legitimately live under one
surrounding whitespace is a typing artefact, never part of a URL
not a URL at all: trimmed and lower-cased rather than thrown, because this runs while building a command line and a bad URL should fail at the REQUEST with a sentence, not here with a stack trace
empty stays empty — the caller decides what an unset server URL means
